newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European stocks weather Greenspan fright.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European stocks weather Greenspan fright.

text.p: European stock and bond markets on Friday clawed back at least some of Thursday's losses, despite the interest rates worries that dominated investor sentiment.
Stock markets on both sides of the Atlantic saw volatile conditions on the back of the expiration of index futures and options contracts in London and the United States.
By the time European bourses closed, the Dow Industrial Average was steady after declining 20 points, led lower by a selloff in the shares of Eastman Kodak and tobacco company Philip Morris.
In Europe investors regained some of their nerve after Thursday's turmoil, sparked by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's hint about an impending rise in U.S. interest rates.
London strategists said the market had probably already taken into account a quarter-point rate rise next week after the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets on Tuesday.
European share markets were helped in part by the dollar, which firmed at first against the mark and yen before faltering in the afternoon.
The strength of the dollar was one of the factors cited by Paris traders behind a 1.3 percent rebound in France's blue chip CAC-40 index.
Traders said prices retreated in the late afternoon as the Dow softened and the dollar consolidated some of its gains.
Appliance manufacturer SEB surged 7.72 percent at 1,018 francs on plans to buy Arno of Brazil.
The story in Frankfurt was similar. The DAX 30 index closed floor trade up 1.03 percent at 3,298.24, but profit-taking eroded later computerised trade.
The volume leader in afternoon trade was telecoms giant Deutsche Telekom, which rose 1.19 marks, or more than three percent, to 39.89 marks.
Among Europe's smaller bourses, rises ranged from 2.39 percent in Amsterdam to 1.23 percent in Stockholm and 0.55 in Milan.
The exception among major stock markets was London, where the FTSE 100 ended just 3.3 points down after lurching either side of Thursday's depressed close.
The stock market extended its losing streak of five days, the FTSE having lost 169 points since last Friday.

"We've been increasing our cash position in the first quarter, getting ready for what could be a very difficult year, and it's only just begun," said David Kidd, chief investment officer fund managers Cantrade.
British political worries also continued to dog the market, with interest rates on hold only until after the national election on May 1.

"If you see a market heading down with an election due, do you want to step up and buy?" asked David Bruce, a director at Abbey Life Investment Services. "I suspect a lot of the weakness we are seeing in the UK is because people are not buying because of the election."

Shares in B.A.T Industries recovered from an early tumble after a U.S. legal settlement by tobacco firm Liggett Group Inc sent tobacco shares sliding in the United States. B.A.T said the settlement would not force it to follow suit. The stock ended up 2.5 p at 491.5.
British and German government bond markets edged higher early on, tracking the overnight rebound in U.S. Treasuries, but they ended well below their highs on concerns about next week's FOMC meeting.
"The comments from Greenspan appear to greenlight a move higher on Tuesday," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank in London.

The dollar, which rocketed to session highs of 1.6946 marks and 123.73 yen after Greenspan's comments, ended European business down nearly one pfennig at 1.6835 marks from Thursday's close. Against the yen it was down at 122.55 yen from 123.64.
Dealers said they expected the dollar to remain supported ahead of the FOMC meeting as markets bet the Fed will hike rates for the first time in two years.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.6835 marks and 122.55 yen, down from 1.6916 marks and 123.74 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS -- CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended down 3.3 points, or 0.08 percent, at 4,254.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 33.41 points, or 1.31 percent, at 2,587.13.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 33.57 points, or 1.03 percent, at 3,298.24. In screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX index ended up 41.49 points at 3,288.52.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $352.65, up $1.00 from Thursday. Silver ended unchanged at $5.18.
